why: Three product defects were found by a person on 2026-08-16 (findings 049, 050, and the unbound Ctrl+C) and none of them was reachable by any automated round, because every harness calls the shell directly and none of them went through the product page's own handlers. They were found one at a time, by walking into them. This file turns that into a rule with the same shape as the shell bundle's: every handler and every toolbar action the product page has must be either DRIVEN by a named harness or WAIVED with a reason, and anything else fails the audit. What is uncovered here is where the next one of those defects is.
rule: paths(page) - driven - waived must be empty

driven.how: pressed as a TOOLBAR BUTTON in a sequence where each action being a no-op yields a different final string: type ABCDEFG, delete-backward x2, move-character-left x2, insert X, move-character-right, delete-forward must leave exactly EDITBTNABCXD, and insert-line-break must put a <text:line-break/> in the saved ODT. The break is taken at a LINE END so the new paragraph starts empty and the oracle can be equality rather than startswith -- startswith would pass a delete-forward no-op. The keyboard path (beforeinput) is a separate check; this is the button, which no round had pressed. Mutation `edit-arrows-swapped` must redden it.

pressed as a TOOLBAR BUTTON immediately after undo, which is the check: undo has just taken the insert marker out, so redo putting it back is a statement about redo rather than about whatever the document held before. Read from the SAVED ODT, not from the revision counter. The earlier IME commits are witnesses, so a redo that replayed more than the last edit is not mistaken for a correct one. Two preconditions, both checked rather than assumed: the profile must offer redo (the button's own `hidden`, because `.click()` fires on a hidden button too and pressing a control the product is not offering measures nothing), and the marker must be ABSENT going in, or 'the marker is present' is satisfied by a document that never lost it. Mutation `redo` -- the button wired to a resolved promise -- must redden it. Registered as driven on 2026-08-22, when the ABI 4 link expired the waiver that had covered this path: that waiver's reason was pinned to the v3 manifest hash precisely so it could not survive the artifact that makes redo reachable.

Since 2026-08-21 its DOCUMENT side is also driven by every-inline-format-reaches-the-document, which measured that bold DOES reach the document -- finding 064, which said otherwise, is retracted. This entry's oracle is still the page's cache and still does not cover the document; it is the wrong oracle for a right answer.

pressed ON and then OFF through the product's own toolbar, with a unique marker committed through the product's own insert field after each press and each arm on its own paragraph. The verdict is the SAVED ODT, and EACH ARM IS READ FROM ITS OWN SAVE: each arm is still read at its own time, which is cheap and correct; findings 064 and 065 both claimed a mechanism here and BOTH ARE RETRACTED -- the eight failures were a false negative in inline_styles_of(), which could not see formatting carried on a paragraph's own automatic style, and that is exactly what a marker alone in its paragraph produces. Not aria-pressed either: the page's cache can be written correctly while the document is untouched, and that is a different question from this one. Whether the formatting SURVIVES is asked separately by formatting-survives-the-next-paragraph-break, which passes.

pressed straight after the insert above; the marker text must be GONE from the saved ODT, read from the document rather than from the revision counter, because D1 covers undo through the shell and this is the button. a synthesised InputEvent('beforeinput', {inputType: deleteContentBackward}) on #sink; the oracle is that the page cancels it AND the revision advances, i.e. it reached the engine. The input adapter also listens for beforeinput but drops both delete types as `ignored-input-type` without preventing them, which is why this is not a second handler for the same work -- checked before it was written, after the paste episode.

a File synthesised from a fixture's bytes is assigned to #file and a change event dispatched, through the page's own handler. The oracle is the document the ENGINE ends up holding -- the run saves afterwards and requires text that exists only in the handed-over file, and none from the fixture that was open before. Mutation `open-file` re-opens the fixture while still updating the filename, and is detected.

a different sample is chosen through the product's own picker: the document name becomes the chosen one, the session returns to `ready`, and the new document is actually DRAWN -- ink found ANYWHERE via stable_bands, not at one hardcoded band, because a different sample puts its text on different lines. This is the product's second open on one page and so the only product path near queue-search-after-reopen-wedges. Mutation `sample-picker-does-nothing` must redden it.

all four inline formats turned ON, the product's own #clear-format button clicked, and a marker committed after it: the first marker must carry all four and the second none. Clearing an already-clear document is the no-op a broken button would pass. The precondition is read from MKALLON's OWN save rather than from the post-clear document: asking a cleared document whether every format WAS on asks it about a moment it no longer records, which is why this looked unbuildable. Same mistake as finding 064, one check over.

the product's own recovery button, pressed in the state the product OFFERS it in -- reached through the page's own buttons: click past the end of a line, insert-paragraph-break, then a list action on the new empty paragraph (finding 046's cell). The oracle is that the notice is shown and enabled, that pressing it returns the session to ready, and that the product can save a real ODT afterwards. Mutation `rollback` (wired to undo instead) is detected; mutation `toolbar-drops-the-list-action` proves the NOT_ESTABLISHED branch cannot hide a broken toolbar.

the product's own #open-file button is clicked and must forward exactly one click to the hidden #file input. #file.click is shimmed to be COUNTED rather than performed -- the same technique this runner already uses for download anchors -- so no OS chooser opens and no human is needed. the check cancels the composition and requires the sink back at opacity 0 and 1px -- the half that matters most, since a sink left visible is a box of stale text on top of the document and the user would have to reload. It is `compositionend` and not the `blur` handler that does it here, and the report says so: `afterwards` carries `focused: true`, so the sink never lost focus.

CDP `Input.imeSetComposition` with bopomofo, which drives the renderer's OWN ime path rather than a synthesised CompositionEvent -- so compositionstart fires the way it does for a real input method. The oracle is `the-composition-you-are-typing-is-visible`: at rest the sink is opacity 0 and 1px wide; while composing it is opacity 1, at least 14px wide, and at the SAME left/top as before, because a visible box in the corner of the page is not the user seeing what they type. Mutation `composition-never-shown` renames the handler and must redden it.

same call: the composition text reaches the sink and its width is sized to that text (measured: value ㄊㄞˊ, width 1 -> 38). Covered by the same check and the same mutation, which renames both handlers together -- they are one path in two events and splitting the mutation would let either half rot alone.
a ClipboardEvent on #sink; the check classifies the outcome by which error the clipboard adapter raises

a synthesised ClipboardEvent('cut') on #sink; classified by which error the clipboard adapter raises, exactly like the copy check. The removal half is NOT established: the delete runs only after a successful clipboard write and WebDriver refuses that.

TWO branches now, and both are named because this audit works per LISTENER and cannot see inside one. (1) a synthesised KeyboardEvent('keydown', {key: ArrowLeft}) on #sink; the oracle is the page cancelling it and the status line reporting a dispatched caret move. (2) a REAL Enter and a REAL Shift+Enter delivered through CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent's sibling Input.dispatchKeyEvent, judged by the-enter-key-reaches-the-document on the PARAGRAPH COUNT in the saved ODT -- never on the revision, which advanced on every broken press under finding 067. That arm is CHROME ONLY: only a real key runs the default action that produces `beforeinput`, so a synthesised keydown would pass it on a page where the binding is absent; Firefox reports NOT_ESTABLISHED. Mutation `enter-key-not-bound` disables the branch and the check must go red. STILL NOT EXERCISED in this handler: Ctrl+Z and Ctrl+S. Ctrl+Z's own coverage is the undo check, which presses the button rather than the key.

a REAL mouse click is delivered onto the set-bold button through CDP Input.dispatchMouseEvent, and then two things are read: document.activeElement must still be the editing sink, and text typed straight afterwards -- with NOTHING restoring focus -- must reach the saved document. The check is the-toolbar-gives-the-keyboard-back. A real click is the whole point: HTMLElement.click() runs no default action and therefore never moves focus, so every synthetic press in this file would pass on a page where this is broken -- which is exactly how finding 066 survived until an operator hit it. CHROME ONLY; Firefox has no CDP here and the check reports NOT_ESTABLISHED rather than passing. Mutation `focus` reverts the two lines and the check must go red.
a synthesised PointerEvent on #canvas, through the page's own handler; placeCaret is confirmed by the engine

the desk is narrowed and a resize event dispatched: the canvas backing store must change size AND the document must still be drawn afterwards (725 -> 404 px, ink still found). A relayout that resizes and never repaints leaves a blank page -- finding 062's shape one layer up. Mutation `resize-does-not-repaint` must redden it.

`an-aborted-gesture-stops-selecting`, which as of 2026-08-23 reports a verdict instead of abstaining. A drag is started, moved once, aborted by this listener, and the pointer keeps moving; the arm's selected TEXT (from the engine, through the product's copy path) must be a strict prefix of a control arm that made the same moves with no abort. MEASURED: passes clean (control 11 code points, both abort arms 10) and FAILS under the `gesture-abort-not-wired` mutation, which is what moves this path out of `uncovered`: it can now go red for this listener being gone. THE PREVIOUS REASON HERE WAS WRONG, and it is retracted rather than edited away: it said the harness could not start an extending drag, and the same DRAG was measured the next day producing 12 code points inside one line and 34 across two. The broken part was the OBSERVABLE -- it read whether the four format buttons were disabled, which finding 079 held at false on every run and e2-editor-v7 then broke a second time by offering those buttons for ranges. Findings 079, 080. LIMIT, and it travels with the check's own PASS record: the detection under mutation came via a failure mode the oracle does not describe (the unwired arm selected nothing rather than running to the end), and the margins are unexplained in both directions -- the control's own reach moved 11 -> 6 between two runs. This path is DRIVEN and the abort wiring is not thereby established. See queue-abort-margins-are-unexplained.

uncovered.risk: MEDIUM -- `hideComposition` on the IME sink, added by finding 073. It is the SECOND of the two endings, and the one that gets forgotten: `compositionend` covers a composition that finishes, `blur` covers one the user walks away from. If it regresses, the sink stays at opacity 1 with stale bopomofo on top of the document and only a reload clears it -- worse than the defect 073 fixed. UNDRIVEN, and the neighbouring entry says so precisely rather than by omission: `the-composition-you-are-typing-is-visible` reports `focused: true` in its `afterwards` block, so that arm proves compositionend did the hiding WITH THE SINK STILL FOCUSED and therefore never touches this path. The route to driving it exists and is cheap -- the same CDP `Input.imeSetComposition` machinery, then take focus away instead of committing -- so this is registered as uncovered because it has not been measured, not because it cannot be.
